deep.reconstruction:
This page opens a section 'Structures stratifiées' and sets up the simplest local model of a two-stratum stratified space. It is the start of Grothendieck's programme of reconstructing a stratified space from its strata plus gluing data, the 'dévissage' of stratified structures sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5.

The data: a closed embedding Y ⊂ X of spaces. The parenthetical says the objects may more generally be other 'espaces' that become topoi; the word is illegible.

The hypothesis is that the 'normal structure' of X along Y is locally trivial. For every y ∈ Y there is:
- an open neighbourhood X' of y,
- a pointed space (Z, z),
- a homeomorphism X' ≅ Y' × Z, with Y' = Y ∩ X', carrying Y' onto Y' × {z} by the canonical map.

In other words, the pair (X, Y) is locally a product of the stratum with a transverse 'normal slice' (Z, z). This is the topological local-triviality or equisingularity condition along a stratum, as in Whitney/Thom–Mather stratifications. There Z is a cone c(L) on a link and z is the cone point.

Grothendieck then introduces the '(infinitesimal) tubular neighbourhood' V_{Y,X}, giving a factorisation Y → V_{Y,X} → X, and says it needs a technically simple definition.

The next page proposes, provisionally, the germ of X along Y: as a topos, the projective limit of the topoi of open neighbourhoods of Y. Intuitively V → X behaves like an open immersion and Y → V like a closed immersion. The key intuition is that Y → V_{Y,X} is a homotopy equivalence under local triviality plus tameness ('modération').

The goal stated there: when Y and X* = X − Y are manifolds and z is a singular point of Z, reconstruct X from the manifolds Y and X*. Implicitly this uses the deleted neighbourhood V* = V ∩ X* and its fibration over Y with fibre the link (the 'bout' of the Esquisse).
errors: Z and the trivialisation depend on y. Only the germ of (Z, z) is meaningful, and Z is not shown to be locally constant along Y (true on connected components once germs are compared, but not argued).

That Y → V_{Y,X} is a homotopy equivalence (next page) needs Z to be locally contractible to z, e.g. conical, plus tameness. Local triviality alone does not give this, which Grothendieck acknowledges with 'moyennant des conditions de modération'.
'Infinitesimal tubular neighbourhood' as a germ is a pro-object (a limit of topoi). Homotopy-theoretic statements about it must be read pro-homotopically (shape); this is not addressed here.

ideas.what: Closed stratum Y ⊂ X with locally trivial normal structure: locally X' ≅ (Y ∩ X') × Z, with Y corresponding to Y × {z}
ideas.modern_name: Topological local triviality / equisingularity along a stratum; normal slice; locally cone-like (CS) stratified sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (1960s–70s); Siebenmann (locally cone-like stratified sets, 1972)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6 (tame topology, dévissage of stratified structures), in informal form

ideas.what: Canonical factorisation Y → V_{Y,X} → X through a 'tubular neighbourhood' that is a germ (on the next page realised as a limit of topoi of open neighbourhoods), behaving like closed immersion followed by open immersion
ideas.modern_name: Germ / pro-neighbourhood of a closed subspace; shape of the germ; relation to the homotopy link (Quinn) and to the oriented product / vanishing topos Y ×_X X*
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tubular neighbourhoods: Whitney, Thom, Mather. Homotopy links: Quinn (1988). Oriented products: Deligne, Laumon, Gabber. Exit-path / ∞-categorical approach: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tubular neighbourhoods and the 'bout' in stratified tame spaces; the topos-germ formulation is not, to my knowledge, published

ideas.what: Programme to reconstruct X from the strata Y, X* and gluing data
ideas.modern_name: Recollement / gluing of stratified spaces; stratified homotopy hypothesis; links as gluing data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mather (control data), Quinn, Hughes, Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (dévissage of stratified structures)

missed.claim: Grothendieck models the tubular neighbourhood purely topos-theoretically, as the germ topos lim of open neighbourhoods of Y. Applying the same construction to X* gives a topos-theoretic deleted tubular neighbourhood. This is closely related to the Deligne–Gabber oriented product Y ×_X X* (vanishing topos) and to Quinn's homotopy link, though this page does not make that link explicitly. The literature on stratified homotopy theory (Quinn, Lurie, AFT) and on vanishing topoi developed largely independently. Grothendieck's framing, 'espaces' that become topoi, suggests a unified topos-level dévissage of stratified spaces that is not standard.
missed.quote: On considère donc "le voisinage tubulaire" ("infinitésimal") de Y dans X, soit (3) Y ↪ V_{Y,X} ↪ X, dont il faudra donner une définition
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A topos-theoretic definition of tubular germs and links would give a common framework for stratified homotopy theory (exit paths, conically smooth spaces) and étale/vanishing-cycle formalisms. This is relevant to current work on stratified shapes and on 'tame' or o-minimal homotopy theory.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the standard local-triviality setup for stratified spaces, already sketched informally in the Esquisse. The only mildly notable point is the intended topos-germ definition of the tubular neighbourhood, which is developed on the next page rather than here.
transcription_corrections: Line 3–4: 'qui se deviennent des topos' is more plausibly 'qui se devinent des topos' or similar. The quoted word before it is illegible in the image; '"bandes"' is doubtful.
'existe une voisinage ouvert' → 'existe un voisinage ouvert'.
The struck '-et-' before 'un espace Z pointé par z' is a crossed-out 'et' at line start; the reading is fine.
In (2) the bottom arrow label reads id_{Y'} × i_{z,Z}; the vertical arrows are isomorphisms (≀), the left one labelled 'can'. The transcription is correct.
